text:
incident-bot: Paging: p99 latency spike observed on /v1/generate (cont-batch path) in us-west-2. Alert threshold breached: p99 > 1.5s for 3m. Severity: P1. @sasha @mike oncall please ack

sasha: acked. jumping in. seeing alert graph in ops dashboard. p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 2.1s right now.

mike: i'm on my way, grabbing logs. does this correlate with increased QPS?

anika: i see mixing of very long seq len requests and short ones — batcher seqlen distribution skewed. could be amplification.

sasha: mike, can you confirm which pool? looks like cont-batch GPU pool gw-3b, job-id batcher-7.

mike: confirmed gw-3b. NODES: g3-4, queue depth spike around 23:10 UTC. QPS up ~15% but not huge. tail latency disproportionate.

luis: adding context from telemetry: KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 60% around onset. evictions spiked. likely mixing large few-shot inputs evicting prefixes.

kate: any customer pages? alice-cs?

alice-cs: two customers reported slow responses (enterprise chatbots). They saw timeouts at 30s for streaming endpoints. I've opened CS tickets and informed them we're investigating.

ops-bot: Automated mitigation suggestion: reduce `max_batch_size` for cont-batch to 32 and enable seqlen-weighted fairshare. Would you like me to apply? Reply `yes` to proceed.

sasha: do the mitigation. also drop streaming queue timeout to 10s to avoid timeouts piling up and blocking sockets.

mike: applying patch now: `kubectl set env ds/batcher MAX_BATCH_SIZE=32 --namespace=batching` -> rolling restart.

anika: while that rolls, we should also change scheduler policy to seqlen-weighted so 1-20 token requests don't get starved by 10k token requests. Patch suggestion:

```yaml
scheduler:
  policy: seqlen_weighted_fairshare
  weights:
    short: 1.0
    long: 0.2
  preemptive_shed: true
```

sasha: +1. mike please apply config to canary first (gw-3b-canary) then roll.

mike: canary patched. monitoring metrics.

incident-bot: Update: `max_batch_size` decreased to 32 on 30% of nodes. KV cache warming in progress.

luis: early signal: p99 down to 1.4s on canary, KV hit up to 74%. Good sign.

kate: are we seeing streaming stalls specifically? any `stalling` traces in the runtime?

anika: yes, traces show streaming stalled waiting for prefix KV loads for >500ms in some RPCs. That matches the eviction theory.

sasha: temporary mitigation: enable short-request priority by threshold `seq_len <= 64` -> fast-path. ops-bot, can you flip a flag for that?

ops-bot: Flag toggled: `fast_path_short_reqs=true` on canary nodes.

mike: full rollout of `max_batch_size=32` and `fast_path_short_reqs` to all nodes started. rolling completes at 23:24 UTC.

incident-bot: Signals 5m post-mitigation: p95 ~ 380ms, p99 ~ 820ms. Streaming stall errors reduced by 85%.

alice-cs: updated customers: informing them latency improved; offering postmortem once complete. They asked whether this will recur.

anika: root cause summary we have so far: mixed sequence lengths causing KV cache churn + large max batch size delaying short requests (queueing amplification) -> paging. Need permanent changes: lower default max_batch_size for cont-batch, implement seqlen-aware batching, and KV cache size tuning / nuke large prefix caching for ephemeral long-context requests.

luis: also recommend proactive alert: add `p99_per_seq_len_bucket` to detect regressions before global p99 crosses SLO.

sasha: agree. action items:
- mike: roll PR to make `max_batch_size` default 32 for cont-batch (prod config), add canary rollout script.
- anika: implement seqlen-weighted scheduler + unit tests, run perf bench.
- luis: increase KV cache capacity for gw-3b and add eviction telemetry to syscall logs.
- kate: coordinate CS updates and track impacted customers for RCA.

mike: started PR -> https://git.redwood.internal/p/batch-config/42 (screenshot pinned).

anika: will open PR for scheduler change and include performance runbook for mixed seq workloads.

sasha: handing off to night shift. please keep channel updated if p99 creeps > 1s again. Next oncall is @luis. I'll DM summaries to infra leads.

luis: acked, will monitor. leaving detailed todo list in the ticket.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated) at 23:30 UTC. Root cause: cont-batch config + KV eviction amplification. Severity downgraded to P2 for RCA.

kate: thanks all. I'll prepare customer-facing postmortem and coordinate timeline.

mike: one more note — we saw small CPU spike on batcher during restart, watched for any regressions. all clear now.

anika: follow-up items created: TKT-2412 (scheduler), TKT-2413 (batch defaults), TKT-2414 (kv telemetry).

sasha: closing paging thread for now. great job team :thumbsup:
